items.name: Sow seeds in a tray
items.about: Start seeds in a shallow tray before moving them to pots.
howToSteps: Fill a tray with fine, moist soil.
Sow seeds about twice as deep as their size.
Keep it moist and in light until they sprout.

items.name: Transplant a seedling
items.about: Move a young plant to its own pot without shocking it.
howToSteps: Water the seedling first.
Lift it with its root ball intact.
Plant at the same depth and water gently.

items.name: Pot a plant properly
items.about: The right pot is half the battle.
howToSteps: Pick a pot with drainage holes.
Add soil, set the plant, and fill around it.
Leave space at the top for watering.

items.name: Mix your own potting soil
items.about: A simple mix of garden soil, compost and cocopeat.
howToSteps: Mix roughly equal parts soil, compost and cocopeat.
Add a handful of sand for succulents.
Moisten before using.

items.name: Water the right way
items.about: Most plants die from too much water, not too little.
howToSteps: Push a finger an inch into the soil.
Water only if it feels dry.
Water deeply until it drains out the bottom.

items.name: Read the light in your space
items.about: Know which spots get full sun, part sun or shade.
howToSteps: Note where sunlight falls at 9 am, 1 pm and 4 pm.
Count the hours of direct sun.
Match plants to each spot.
keywords: read the light in your space

items.name: Make kitchen compost
items.about: Turn peels and leaves into rich soil.
howToSteps: Layer vegetable scraps with dry leaves.
Turn it weekly and keep it damp.
Use it when it's dark and crumbly.

items.name: Mulch your pots
items.about: A layer on top keeps soil moist and cool.
howToSteps: Spread dry leaves or coco husk on the soil.
Keep it a little away from the stem.
Top up as it breaks down.

items.name: Pinch and prune
items.about: Cutting tips makes plants bushier.
howToSteps: Pinch the top pair of leaves on basil or tulsi.
Cut just above a leaf node.
Use clean scissors.

items.name: Deadhead flowers
items.about: Remove faded flowers for more blooms.
howToSteps: Snip spent flowers below the bloom.
Do it weekly in the flowering season.
Watch new buds appear.

items.name: Feed with compost or vermicompost
items.about: Plants in pots need regular food.
howToSteps: Add a handful of compost every few weeks.
Mix it into the top layer of soil.
Water well afterwards.

items.name: Spray neem against pests
items.about: A gentle natural way to keep pests away.
howToSteps: Mix a little neem oil and soap in water.
Spray under the leaves in the evening.
Repeat weekly if pests return.

items.name: Repot a root-bound plant
items.about: Give a cramped plant a bigger home.
howToSteps: Look for roots coming out of the bottom.
Move it to a pot one size bigger.
Loosen the roots gently before replanting.

items.name: Support a climber
items.about: Help gourds, beans and money plants climb.
howToSteps: Add sticks, a net or a string up a railing.
Guide the tendrils onto it.
Tie gently with soft string if needed.

items.name: Make a self-watering bottle
items.about: Reuse a plastic bottle to water slowly.
howToSteps: Poke small holes in a bottle cap.
Fill it and push it upside down into the soil.
Refill as it empties.

items.name: Take a stem cutting
items.about: Make a new plant from a piece of the old one.
howToSteps: Cut 10–15 cm below a leaf node.
Remove the lower leaves.
Root it in water or moist soil.

items.name: Grow from kitchen scraps
items.about: Regrow spring onion, ginger or mint from the kitchen.
howToSteps: Keep the root end of a spring onion.
Stand it in water for a few days.
Plant it once new shoots appear.

items.name: Divide a plant
items.about: Split an overgrown plant into two.
howToSteps: Take the plant out of its pot.
Gently pull or cut the clump apart.
Pot each part separately.

items.name: Save your own seeds
items.about: Keep seeds from this season for the next.
howToSteps: Let a healthy fruit or flower fully ripen.
Dry the seeds in the shade.
Store them in a labelled paper packet.

items.name: Make seed balls
items.about: Clay-and-compost balls to scatter seeds.
howToSteps: Mix clay, compost and a few seeds with a little water.
Roll into small balls and dry them.
Toss them on bare ground before the monsoon.

items.name: Try air layering
items.about: Root a branch while it's still on the plant.
howToSteps: Remove a ring of bark on a healthy branch.
Wrap it in moist moss and plastic.
Cut and pot it once roots show.

items.name: Hand-pollinate flowers
items.about: Help gourds and squash set fruit on a terrace.
howToSteps: Find a male flower (no tiny fruit behind it).
Brush its pollen onto a female flower.
Do it in the morning.

items.name: Start vermicomposting
items.about: Let earthworms make rich compost.
howToSteps: Set up a bin with moist bedding and worms.
Feed vegetable scraps, not dairy or oil.
Harvest the compost after a few months.

items.name: Collect rainwater for the garden
items.about: Save monsoon rain for drier days.
howToSteps: Place a bucket or drum under a downpipe.
Cover it to keep mosquitoes out.
Use it to water your plants.

items.name: Shape a bonsai
items.about: Prune and wire a small tree into shape.
howToSteps: Choose a branch structure you like.
Prune unwanted branches gradually.
Wire lightly and remove before it cuts in.
